content: Have you ever wondered what happens to that delicious slice of pizza after you swallow it? It disappears into your body, but you never see it again. Where does it go, and how does your body turn it into the energy that lets you run and play?
If a piece of food is solid, how does it travel through your blood to reach your toes? What must your body do to the food before it can be used?

Imagine your body is a giant recycling factory. You can't just throw a whole car into the final mold. You have to break it down into smaller pieces of metal first. Similarly, your digestive system is a 9-meter long tube that acts as a food crushing and chemical dissolving factory!

content.title: The Human Digestive Tract
content.description: An animated journey of a piece of food travelling from the mouth, down the esophagus, into the churning stomach, and through the winding intestines.

content: This process of breaking down complex food substances into simpler, soluble substances is called Digestion (पाचन - Pachan). Let's look at the key concepts involved.

question: What is the main purpose of digestion?
options: To break down complex food into simpler substances
To mix food with water only

content: Think about this: Why do we need to chew our food so many times? What would happen if we just swallowed everything whole?
Chewing your food 32 times isn't just a myth! It mechanically breaks down food and mixes it with saliva, which contains enzymes that start digesting carbohydrates right in your mouth!

How does this connect to other things? Just like plants use photosynthesis to make their food, animals must ingest and digest. Your digestive system works with your circulatory system: once food is broken down in the small intestine, the blood absorbs it and carries the nutrients to every cell in your body.

Challenge: Take a piece of plain bread and chew it for a full minute without swallowing. Do you notice it starting to taste sweet? That's the enzymes in your saliva breaking down complex starches into simple sugars right in your mouth! You are witnessing digestion in action.

Many students think the stomach is where most digestion and absorption happens. In reality, the small intestine is the superstar where the majority of digestion and almost all absorption of nutrients takes place!
